subject: PO structure, invoice rhythm & volume discounts for HorizonTech
messages:
From: Susan Lopez <susan.lopez@horizontech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts-payable@horizontech.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood: PO structure question + net terms

Hi Karthik,

We're moving to finalize the procurement packet for Redwood but Finance flagged two items they need clarity on before issuing the PO: 1) HorizonTech prefers consolidated monthly invoices (one invoice per month) but our internal ERP needs each purchase line attributed to a department code — is it possible to provide a single monthly invoice with line-level PO references? 2) We typically do net45 for vendors of this size; your standard is net30 — any flexibility there?

Also, on discounts: our procurement lead asked whether discount tiers can be applied against annual committed usage (we anticipate a 12-month consumption estimate, but purchase will be through monthly invoicing). Can you confirm whether discounts can be applied retroactively to meet tier thresholds, or must they be applied at invoice time?

Attaching a sample PO template they want to use (we renamed some fields).

Thanks,
Susan Lopez
Sr. Procurement Manager 
HorizonTech

Attachments: HorizonTech_PO_78923.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lopez <susan.lopez@horizontech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood: PO structure question + net terms

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear ask and for the PO template. Short answers up front: yes on a single monthly invoice with line-level PO references; we can map to your department codes on the invoice. Net45 is possible but needs a brief approval from Finance for this account (we typically allow net45 for enterprise deals with an executed commitment). On discounts: we support a volume tiering model measured monthly but reconciled quarterly for retroactive true-ups — we can either: (A) apply provisional invoice pricing and then issue a credit for any retroactive tier discount at quarter close, or (B) set committed-tier pricing up front and invoice at that tier.

A few items I need from your side to get Finance to approve net45 and to lock in the paperwork:
- Estimated ARR or monthly spend cadence (ballpark numbers are fine)
- Whether you need the discount to be applied prospectively (option B) or allow interim true-ups (option A)
- Any SAP/ERP PO field mapping specifics (they mentioned department code and cost center)

I've looped in Marissa (finance) to confirm the approval path and to propose the crediting workflow. I also attached a short draft SOW with our recommended billing labels.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0194

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf); Discount_Tiers_Proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Susan Lopez <susan.lopez@horizontech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood: PO structure question + net terms

Hi Susan / Karthik — happy to take this one. From Finance's perspective: we can approve net45 for HorizonTech pending an executed order (signed SOW + PO) and a standard credit review. For invoice structure: we can emit a single consolidated invoice each month that includes line items with PO references mapped to your department codes; our billing system supports up to 10 custom fields per line for ERP mapping (please send the exact field names).

Regarding discounts: the cleanest approach operationally is option B (set committed-tier pricing at contract signature). That avoids frequent credits and manual reconciliations. If HorizonTech prefers option A (provisional pricing with quarterly true-up), we can accommodate it but we'll need your AP team to accept quarterly credits and offsetting journal entries — some of our customers have longer vendor reconciliation cycles which complicates things.

If you want an exception to always apply retroactive credits monthly, that requires a manual process and an admin fee to cover the reconciliation effort. If you can share your expected monthly consumption range, we can model both approaches and show the delta.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik: get the 12-month consumption estimate (order of magnitude)
- Susan: confirm preferred credit model (A: quarterly true-up, B: committed-tier upfront)
- Marissa/Finance will prepare a net45 exception memo and the billing field mapping template

Thanks — copying Ben for visibility on discount approvals.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Lopez <susan.lopez@horizontech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood: PO structure question + net terms

Susan — appreciated the clear framing. We've reviewed the ask and can offer the following commercial concession to help close the deal this quarter:

1) Net45 approved for HorizonTech for the first 12 months (subject to signed SOW + PO).
2) Discounting: we will set a committed-tier schedule in the SOW (Tier 1 / Tier 2 breakpoints) and invoice at the committed tier. At quarter close, if actual consumption exceeds the committed tier, we'll apply a retroactive credit for the incremental volume (i.e., hybrid of B with quarterly true-up on incremental volume only).
3) Billing: we will deliver a single monthly consolidated invoice with line-level PO and custom field mapping. We'll need your AP to accept monthly invoice format + quarterly reconciliation credits.

I'll escalate one manual-fee waiver for the initial onboarding reconciliation (we'll absorb that for HorizonTech). Marissa, please prepare the formal net45 exception memo and attach the billing-field template Karthik requested.

Susan — if that aligns, please confirm and we'll share an updated SOW + credit process doc and a DocuSign envelope for the signature.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Ops 
Redwood Inference
